President of Liberia from 1944 until his death in 1971, the longest in its history.

His Open Door policy brought foreign companies to mine iron ore and grow rubber, and the economy grew fast in the 1950s, though wealth stayed with a few. His unification policy gave people of the interior the vote and some seats in government, and women got the vote. He kept tight personal control through the True Whig Party, patronage and a secret police. Abroad he was a founder of the Organisation of African Unity. His successor William Tolbert was killed in the 1980 coup. See also the shipping registry.
sum: President of Liberia from 1944 until his death in 1971, the longest in its history.
